blocks.text: Langley mobile home parks: the six parks and the rules

parts.t: Park rules are not strata bylaws, there is no strata corporation, and there is no Form B for a pad-rental purchase. All six parks below are in the Township of Langley; none is in the City of Langley.

items.t: Fernridge Park — 20071 24 Avenue, Brookswood (Township): Directory: 55+ grouping, pets not allowed.
Pineridge Estates / Pine Ridge Park — 2270 196 Street, Brookswood (Township): Directory: 55+ grouping, pets allowed with limits.
Deer Creek Estates — 2315 198 Street, Brookswood (Township): Directory: 55+ grouping, one pet allowed with restrictions.
Aldergrove Mobile Home Park — 26892 Fraser Highway, Aldergrove (Township).
Cedar Springs Mobile Home Park — 23387 70A Avenue, Salmon River (Township)

parts.t: Age and pet rules above come from recent MLS® listings. Confirm them, and the current pad rent, with the park manager before you write an offer. "Pineridge Estates" and "Pine Ridge Park" are the same park at 2270 196 Street, so search both names.

blocks.text: How owning a park home works

items.t: How ownership works in a park: many residents own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.

Selling a park home means assigning the pad tenancy to the buyer, which permanently transfers it. You need the landlord's written consent first (or a director's order, or permission in the tenancy agreement). The landlord can't charge a fee for consenting, and the pad rent and the date of the next increase stay the same for the buyer.

Registration and certification: in BC a manufactured home sale/transfer is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry (lawyer/notary filing the signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership); a home may not be sold without its original legible CSA decal (Z-240 mobile homes, A-277 modular), and a lost label requires Technical Safety BC re-certification.

Taxes on a park home: a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner — the tax treatment itself confirms the pad is not the buyer's land.

MHPTA site tenancies require a written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement. Pad-rent increases: only with 3 full months' written notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit — 2026: 2.3% plus a proportional amount; 2027: 2.2% plus a proportional amount. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park. The landlord may not round up and may not carry forward an unused portion of a prior year's limit. These percentages are the only pad-rent figures an official source gives — no dollar figure is stated.

The proportional amount means two parks rise differently in the same year: it is each park's own levy + regulated-utility change divided by that park's own site count, so the same 2.3% headline for 2026 produces a different dollar increase at Fernridge Park than at Cedar Creek Estates. Ask the specific park for its last calculation.
Schools (SD35): Brookswood Secondary, 20902 37a Ave, in the Brookswood-Fernridge cluster this page leads with; Aldergrove Community Secondary, 26850 29 Ave, in Aldergrove.
Transit: the page states Deer Creek Estates has "a bus stop at the park entrance" and describes Aldergrove Mobile Home Park as "close to transit".

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Communities: how mobile and manufactured homes work here

items.t: Grouping on the page: four parks grouped as "55+ Mobile Home Parks in Brookswood-Fernridge" in south Langley near 200 Street and 24 Avenue, plus two grouped as "All-Ages Mobile Home Parks in Langley" (Aldergrove and Salmon River). All six addresses are in the Township of Langley; none is in the City of Langley.

Schools: Brookswood Secondary (20902 37a Ave) is the Ministry-listed secondary in the Brookswood-Fernridge cluster; Aldergrove Community Secondary (26850 29 Ave) is the confirmed secondary in Aldergrove. These are physical locations, not catchment claims.
The two Langley topic pages' park sets overlap only partially: A reader using this directory alone would miss most parks with homes actually listed.

faq.q: Is a home in one of these communities a condo?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the MHPTA. There is no strata corporation, no strata fees and no Form B.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in these parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change. This page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions" — all taken from recent listings.

faq.q: A park here says 55+ — is that the same 55+ bylaw as a condo?
faq.a: In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw with exemptions set by law. In a park, 55+ is a rule in the park's written rules; the strata exemptions don't apply, and the park's wording decides. Get the park rules in writing before you remove subjects.

faq.q: Is a home in one of these communities a townhouse?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement governed by the MHPTA.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in these parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change. This page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions" — all taken from recent listings.

faq.q: A park here says 55+ — is that the same 55+ bylaw as a strata townhouse?
faq.a: In a strata, 55+ is a registered bylaw with exemptions set by law. In a park, 55+ is a rule in the park's written rules; the strata exemptions don't apply, and the park's wording decides.

faq.q: How much can pad rent go up each year?
faq.a: Up to the Residential Tenancy Branch limit for manufactured home site tenancies: 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, on 3 full months' notice, once every 12 months.

faq.q: If I buy a home in one of these parks, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the manufactured home and rent the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement (MHPTA); your property tax assessment in a park excludes the land's value for exactly that reason.

faq.q: In a pad-rental park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home and rent the pad; your right to the site is the pad tenancy assigned to you. Pioneer Park in Aldergrove is the exception: it's a co-op.

faq.q: How much is pad rent in these parks?
faq.a: The figure that matters is the specific park's current rent in its written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement.

faq.q: Does a park have to approve me, and does my rent reset when I buy?
faq.a: Approval: yes — prior written consent on RTB Form 10, response by the 10th day, silence deemed consent, no fee. Reset: no — on assignment the pad rent stays the same and the next increase date does not change.

faq.q: What should I check before anything else on a park home?
faq.a: The CSA label — without the original legible CSA decal the home cannot be sold until Technical Safety BC re-certification — and the Manufactured Home Registry record, since the sale is only effective once registered.

faq.q: What are the age and pet rules in Langley parks?
faq.a: Park by park, and they can change — this page lists its four Brookswood-Fernridge parks as 55+ and its Aldergrove and Salmon River parks as all-ages, with pet rules ranging from "not allowed" to "allowed with restrictions," all taken from recent listings.

faq.q: How much can a park raise pad rent each year?
faq.a: Up to the Residential Tenancy Branch limit for manufactured home site tenancies: 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, on 3 full months' notice, once every 12 months. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of sites in the park.
